findings.title: The Ads sync deterministically replays one completed 90-day window instead of advancing
findings.cause: The per-slice cap returns a resume cursor before checking whether the current page has a next cursor. When the terminal page crosses the cap, the serialized resume has a window start but no next page. The next slice starts that window from page one again.
findings.impact: Paid KPIs and campaign reporting stop at September 12 while scheduled provider work continues every ten minutes.
findings.repair: On a terminal page, advance to the next window or target before returning a resume cursor; finish when no successor exists. Add a regression where a terminal page crosses the row cap and prove the first page is never replayed.

findings.title: The UI reports connection and sync activity without exposing the stale paid-data boundary
findings.impact: A user sees Active, receives Sync started after any 2xx response, and cannot see the old queued Ads job because high-frequency tail jobs displace it from the newest-20 table. Dashboard widgets combine data with different freshness dates and provide no as-of label.
findings.repair: Show active jobs ahead of recent terminal history, parse per-kind sync results, poll or refresh until terminal, and display the paid, post, and message freshness boundaries on the relevant surfaces.

findings.title: Campaign lead attribution is a July heuristic snapshot, while the UI presents it as an ongoing lead feed
findings.impact: Campaign pages label the rows as leads from this campaign and show confidence, but omit provenance and capture freshness. Operators can treat a one-time model-derived backfill as current exact attribution.
findings.repair: Either qualify and wire the exact gateway referral relay, or explicitly label the current rows as a July heuristic snapshot. Display provenance and data-through time before using these counts for campaign decisions.

findings.title: Successful post and message jobs conceal partial collection
findings.impact: Green job status does not mean all targets or metrics were collected. The top-post score sums whatever metrics happen to exist, so FACES ranks Instagram reactions/comments against Facebook shares and the current top five are all Instagram.
findings.repair: Introduce complete, partial, and failed outcome states per target and metric family. Define a comparable ranking metric or separate platform leaderboards, and show missing-permission coverage in the UI.

findings.title: Sync failures retain and expose unbounded provider error payloads
findings.impact: A future failure can add a very large raw provider string to the page payload, search index, rendered table, and export. The current retained errors had no access-token, authorization, app-secret-proof, URL, or HTML markers, but size remains uncontrolled.
findings.repair: Persist a bounded operator-safe summary and error class with a correlation id. Keep full diagnostics only in a size-bounded restricted log.

strengths: All nine expected Meta and message read-model tables exist in production.
Four assets are enabled: one ad account, two Instagram assets, and one page; paid currency resolves consistently to PEN.
All 1084 observed post-media rows are mirrored with zero retained media errors.
Instagram message ingestion was current within minutes of the probe.
Unauthenticated Socials routes redirect to login and the read API rejects missing authentication.
The dashboard grid has a source-defined single-column container fallback below 620px.
limitations: No authenticated browser session was used; rendered visual behavior is not certified.
No provider-side token introspection or Meta API call was made.

Vercel inspection confirmed a READY production deployment but did not expose its source revision. Source causality is therefore an inference supported by the matching live job progression, not a deployment-SHA attestation.
The timeout-aborted aggregate attempt wrote nothing because the transaction was read only; the final receipt completed all 21 bounded probes.
